run.question:
Alertmanager alert HighRequestErrorRate (severity critical) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-25T16:19:59Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The alert is firing because the frontend's gRPC calls to the ad service are being refused at the network level. In the window sampled from 2026-11-25T16:16:00Z, frontend error-span rate was 0 at 16:16:00 and 16:18:00 and rose to 1.409 at 16:20:00 and 5.511 at 16:22:00, matching the alert value 5.1778; the frontend spans that carry the error are GET /api/data (http.status_code 500), executing api route (pages) /api/data, and the client span oteldemo.AdService/GetAds with rpc.grpc.status_code 14 and exception message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.115.246:8080.' The refused address 10.96.115.246 is the ClusterIP of Service otel-demo/ad, whose spec now maps port 8080 to targetPort 8083 and port 9465 to targetPort 9468, while the ad Deployment's container listens on 8080 (AD_PORT=8080) and 9465 (AD_PROMETHEUS_PORT=9465). The ad Service's last recorded write was an Update by manager 'OpenAPI-Generator' at 2026-11-25T16:18:59Z, the same instant the ad pod's log stream stops receiving ad requests (newest ad log line 16:18:59.358Z) and ad's own span rate for oteldemo.AdService/GetAds falls from 1.0889 to 0. The ad pod itself is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and logged only normal ad request handling, so this is not a pod crash; the fault is the Service's targetPort mapping. frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator show their own error spans/500s consistent with this dependency failure, while the other frontend dependencies I checked show zero error spans.

claims.text: The alerting rule HighRequestErrorRate in rule group opentelemetrydemo.frontend.goldensignal is in state firing with activeAt 2026-11-25T16:19:59Z for service_name=frontend (value 5.177777777777777) and for service_name=frontend-proxy (value 2.2555555555555555); its query is sum by (service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{namespace="otel-demo",service_name=~"frontend|frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[2m])) > 0 with duration 180s.

Last error: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.115.246:8080. Resolution note: ' and the /api/data spans carry the same exception.message.

Frontend error-span rate was 0 at the sampled points 16:16:00Z and 16:18:00Z and became non-zero from the 16:20:00Z sample (1.4091), reaching 5.5111 at 16:22:00Z; by span name the non-zero error series are GET /api/data (2.5778 at 16:22:59Z), executing api route (pages) /api/data (1.2889) and oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (1.2889), plus tcp.connect (0.0222).

Service otel-demo/ad has ClusterIP 10.96.115.246 (the address that frontend's error message reports as refused) and its ports are 9465 -> targetPort 9468 (name prometheus) and 8080 -> targetPort 8083 (name tcp-service); its last managedFields entry is {manager: OpenAPI-Generator, operation: Update, time: 2026-11-25T16:18:59Z}, after the Helm Apply entry at pod-creation time 2026-11-25T16:11:28Z.

Deployment otel-demo/ad runs image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-ad with env AD_PORT=8080 and AD_PROMETHEUS_PORT=9465 and containerPorts 8080 (name service) and 9465 (name prometheus); these values do not match the ad Service's targetPorts 8083 and 9468.

The ad Service's Endpoints object resolves pod ad-6478f46d8-fd76c (10.244.2.30, node kind-environment-worker, uid ca7dbee5-5866-49c8-834b-ae2c8d687732) with ports 8083 (tcp-service) and 9468 (prometheus), i.e. the Service does have a ready backend pod but forwards to ports 8083/9468.

Pod ad-6478f46d8-fd76c is Running, its container is Ready with 0 restarts, and its newest log line inside the query window is 2026-11-25T16:18:59.358Z ('oteldemo.AdService - Targeted ad request received for [books]'); the ad container has no previous instance, and the lines read contain only normal ad request handling.

Ad's own span rate for oteldemo.AdService/GetAds fell from 1.0889 (16:18:59Z sample) to 0.7778, 0.3 and then 0 at the 16:21:59Z and 16:22:59Z samples, and ad's GET /metrics span rate also reached 0 at 16:21:59Z and 16:22:59Z.

Frontend pod frontend-5c847cc9bd-bd847 logged repeated '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.115.246:8080.' errors from the getAds client path, with shown lines running from 2026-11-25T16:22:54.321Z to 2026-11-25T16:23:06.614Z.

Among the 24 Services in otel-demo, ad is the only one whose last managedFields write is at or after 2026-11-25T16:15:00Z (OpenAPI-Generator Update at 16:18:59Z); the other 23 Services show no such recent write.

frontend-proxy spans in the same traces show GET and 'router frontend egress' with error=true and http.status_code 500, and load-generator spans show GET with error=true and http.status_code 500, while load-generator's user_get_ads spans are not_recorded.

The ad workload itself is not failing on its own terms: pod ad-6478f46d8-fd76c is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, has no previous container instance, and its log lines in the read window show normal 'Targeted ad request'/'Non-targeted ad request' handling up to 16:18:59Z; its error-span series for span_name flagd.evaluation.v2.Service/ResolveBoolean stays at 0 throughout the sampled points.

A cluster-network-policy explanation is not supported by what was checked: the query for NetworkPolicy objects in otel-demo returned zero objects at query time, and the ad Service has a populated Endpoints subset pointing at the ready ad pod.

Rejected: an ad pod crash, eviction or restart caused the outage. The ad pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and no previous container instance, all otel-demo pod events in the window are Normal Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started entries plus one otel-collector startup readiness miss, and the refusing error is a TCP connection-refused at the Service ClusterIP:8080 level rather than an application error from ad.

Other frontend dependencies showed no error spans in the sampled error-rate series: the per-service/per-span error rate query returned 0 for cart (POST, flagd EventStream/ResolveBoolean), checkout, product-catalog, recommendation, currency (via the frontend's other client spans oteldemo.CartService/*, oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations all at 0), and for accounting/email/payment/shipping-style operations that appeared, while the only non-zero error series belong to frontend, frontend-proxy, load-generator and ad's flagd ResolveBoolean (0).

The only ConfigMaps present in otel-demo are agent-fixtures, flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector, postgresql-init and product-catalog-product-catalog-otel-config; no ConfigMap related to ad exists to hold an ad-specific fault setting.

The proximate cause of the frontend errors is the ad Service's targetPort mapping (8080 -> 8083, 9465 -> 9468) being changed at 2026-11-25T16:18:59Z by the update whose manager is recorded as OpenAPI-Generator: traffic to ad:8080 is DNATed to pod port 8083 where the ad container (AD_PORT=8080) is not listening, producing ECONNREFUSED and, in turn, the frontend /api/data 500s and the alert. The ad pod stops receiving requests at that same instant.

Restore the ad Service port mapping to the ports the ad container actually serves (tcp-service 8080 -> targetPort 8080, prometheus 9465 -> targetPort 9465, or use the named container ports service/prometheus), then confirm with the Endpoints object and with frontend GetAds errors stopping; no pod restart should be required since the ad pod is healthy.

gaps: The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so which actor (beyond the managedFields manager string 'OpenAPI-Generator') issued the 2026-11-25T16:18:59Z update to Service otel-demo/ad, and what its intent was, could not be verified.

No snapshot of Service otel-demo/ad before 16:18:59Z was available: managedFieldsSummary only gives the last write time per manager, not which fields changed, so the previous targetPort values are unknown.

The ad container's actual listening sockets were not directly observed (no exec/probe data available); AD_PORT=8080 / AD_PROMETHEUS_PORT=9465 / containerPort 8080 and 9465, and the fact that no ad request reached the pod after 16:18:59Z, are the supporting evidence.
Pod log reads were limited (newest 60 of 484 matching ad lines and newest 40 of 746 matching frontend lines shown); older lines and rotated/previous-instance output are unknown.

Frontend trace search with limit 30 over 16:00-16:23Z exceeded the view limit (RESULT_TOO_LARGE) and was not paged, so the trace picture comes from the narrower operation-filtered sample only; span counts are a biased sample, not a request or failure rate.
next_steps: Correct the ad Service targetPorts on the cluster and re-check frontend GetAds span status plus GET /api/data error rate against the pre-incident zero baseline (16:16:00Z and 16:18:00Z samples).

Review the automation behind the 'OpenAPI-Generator' manager entry for Service otel-demo/ad to see what wrote targetPorts 8083/9468, and add a validation that Service targetPorts match the ad Deployment's container ports (8080/9465).

Optionally alert on ad Service endpoint-port mismatch or on frontend's oteldemo.AdService/GetAds rpc.grpc.status_code=14 rate, since the backend rule excludes frontend/frontend-proxy and did not flag the ad dependency itself.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.
